title: Catégorie des types de mots [dont arbres plans] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 1-3): Grothendieck studies the combinatorial 'type' of a word of length n in letters and their inverses (u, u^{-1}, ...). The type records the pattern of cancellations under free reduction. The next page makes this explicit. A word is a 'graphe segmenté' (a path with n edges, the letters) carrying an involution σ on the edges, which pairs each letter with its cancellation partner. 'Admissible' is defined recursively: σ = id, or some 2-element orbit consists of two consecutive edges whose contraction gives an admissible involuted graph. In modern terms, the admissible involutions are exactly the non-crossing partial matchings arising from successive adjacent cancellations.

This page gives a topological, isotopy-invariant model of these types.
- Data: a system (D, ω, K, S, S_0). D is a topological disc and ω an orientation. K ⊂ D is a 1-complex, the union of pairwise disjoint chords, i.e. a 'décomposition par cordes' of D into subdiscs. S ⊂ ∂D is a set of n marked points ('sommets'). S_0 is a base point/base arc, and R_0 is the unique component of ∂D \ K containing S_0.
- Axioms: card S = n. Every boundary arc α ∈ π_0(∂D \ (K∩∂D)) meets S. If α ⊄ R_0 then card(S∩α) = 1.
- Reading: chord endpoints are cancelled letters, chords join cancelled pairs, and the points of S are the positions between letters.
- Interpretation of the axioms: an arc carrying several S-points contains uncancelled letters. The rule 'exactly one point off R_0' says that surviving letters all lie at nesting depth 0, outside every cancelled pair, i.e. in the outer region containing the base point. This is precisely the structure of free reduction.
- The 'ordre réduit' is Σ_α (card(α∩S) − 1). It counts the surviving letters, i.e. the length of the reduced word. A trivial word type (the word reduces to 1) is one with ordre réduit = 0. A reduced word type is one with K = ∅ (no cancellation).
- Main claim: the category of 'types de mots' of length n is equivalent to the isotopy category of such chord-decomposed oriented discs.

The upper part of the page records variant dualities:
- 'disques découpés + un rayon fixé' ↔ 'tambour circonscrit ponctué'.
- Chord-decomposed discs ↔ embedded pointed graphs with free ends ('bouts libres') circumscribed by the circle, oriented at an origin.
- Decomposed discs with each region containing at least one (or, alternatively, at most one) vertex ↔ circumscribed trees, i.e. plane trees.

These are the standard planar dualities: regions become vertices and chords become edges of the dual plane tree. The pictures show words such as vu^{-1}u and uvu^{-1}, a star-shaped embedded graph with loops, and the example disc with regions and dots. The purpose is a geometric (planar-tree / chord-diagram) description of the category of word types announced in the cote title 'dont arbres plans'.
errors: The line 'type de mot réduit : K=∅ (i.e. trivial)' seems to conflate two notions: K=∅ means no cancellation (the word is reduced), while 'trivial' was just defined as ordre réduit = 0. Probably 'trivial' here refers to a trivial cancellation structure, but as written it is inconsistent.
Morphisms of the 'category of types of words' are not specified on this page, so the claimed equivalence of categories (rather than a bijection of isotopy classes) is not checkable here.
The final line 'type de mot trivial : si Σ card S∩α ...' is left unfinished.

ideas.what: Cancellation pattern of a word under free reduction encoded as a non-crossing partial matching (involution on letters, admissible by successive adjacent contractions)
ideas.modern_name: Non-crossing (partial) pairings / free reduction diagrams; Catalan combinatorics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Dyck words; Kesten 1959 on random walks on free groups; non-crossing partitions in Kreweras 1972, Speicher/Voiculescu free probability)

ideas.what: Isotopy model: oriented disc with disjoint chords and n marked boundary points, base region R_0, with the axiom that arcs outside R_0 carry exactly one point
ideas.modern_name: Chord diagrams / non-crossing chord decompositions of a marked disc (as in van Kampen-type diagrams for free reduction)

ideas.what: Reduced order = Σ_α (card(α∩S) − 1) equals the length of the reduced word; trivial type iff 0
ideas.modern_name: Length of the freely reduced word

ideas.what: Duality between chord-decomposed discs and circumscribed embedded graphs/trees with free ends (regions with at least one or at most one vertex ↔ trees)
ideas.modern_name: Planar duality between non-crossing chord diagrams and plane trees
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses maps/dessins and plane trees, but not this specific word-type correspondence

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a 'category' of word types (with composition and inversion operations, per the previous page) and asserts its equivalence with an isotopy category of chord-decomposed marked discs. This is a categorical/operadic packaging of free-reduction combinatorics, but the morphisms and the categorical structure are left unspecified.
missed.quote: La cat. des "types de mots" de long. n équivaut à la cat. isotopique des systèmes formés d'un disque D ... d'une "décomposition par cordes"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mildly reminiscent of later planar-tree/chord-diagram categories (e.g. non-crossing partition lattices, dendroidal-type categories). However, the content visible here is standard combinatorics, and no clearly new result can be extracted.

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives a careful topological encoding of free-reduction patterns by chord-decomposed discs and their dual plane trees. This is mathematically correct but classical Catalan/van Kampen combinatorics. The only unusual feature is the categorical framing and its link to Grothendieck's plane-tree program, which remains undeveloped here.
transcription_corrections: 'S_0 vers [?] ... π_0(...)' is likely 'S_0 ∈ π_0(Ḋ \ K∩Ḋ)' (a chosen base arc), with the struck-out alternative 'S_0 un point de ...'.
'un germe [?] orienté' is more plausibly 'un disque D orienté' / 'muni d'une orientation'.
'cordonnés [?] à involution' in the top-right is likely 'cordes...' or 'chaînes (?) à involution', referring to the involuted segmented graphs of the next page; uncertain.
'avec au moins un sommet sur chaque arête découpée sur Ḋ par les extrémités des cordes' should read 'arc', i.e. the components of the boundary minus the chord endpoints.
In the reduced-order formula, the subscript condition reads 'α∈π_0(Ḋ\K∩Ḋ)', with a struck variant '(α ⊂ R_0)'.
